section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence between the Department of State, the Federal Communications Commission, the American Embassy in Tokyo, the American Legation in Bern, and private companies regarding radio frequency interference caused by Japanese stations. The disputes involve interference to RCA, U.S. Navy, and Press Wireless operations, centering on priority rights under the Bern Bureau of the International Telecommunication Union and technical issues like harmonic emissions. The section also includes Japanese efforts in Kobe to persuade American firms to route telegraph traffic over Japanese government wireless systems instead of foreign submarine cables.

subfiles.about: Moore informs Prall of inquiries into ITU Bureau frequency registration rules regarding interference to station KPH Bolinas.
subfiles.summary: State Department transmits Tokyo despatch on KPH interference and explains inquiry into Bern Bureau registration procedures.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Anning S. Prall regarding KPH Bolinas interference
subfiles.to: Anning S. Prall, Chairman, Federal Communications Commission

subfiles.about: State Department asks American Legation in Bern whether omitted registration dates signify priority relinquishment.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether dash entries in ITU frequency list indicate priority relinquishment, specifically for Japanese station on 8440 kc.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 73 to American Legation Bern regarding frequency list priority

subfiles.about: FCC informs State Department regarding the search for an alternate frequency for station KPH.
subfiles.summary: Reports RCA has found no alternate frequency in the 8000 kc band; requests information on Bern Bureau ruling.
subfiles.title: Letter from Anning S. Prall to Secretary of State regarding KPH frequency change

subfiles.about: Legation Bern reports that the ITU Bureau's lengthy reply is being forwarded by mail.
subfiles.from: Hugh R. Wilson, American Minister, Bern
subfiles.summary: Advises that the Telegraph Bureau's extensive reply has been forwarded by mail on the steamship Queen Mary.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 84 from Bern regarding ITU Bureau reply

subfiles.about: Moore notifies Prall that the Bern Bureau statement has been dispatched by mail.
subfiles.summary: Informs FCC that the Bern Bureau explanation was mailed from Europe on October 26 via SS Queen Mary.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Anning S. Prall regarding Bern report mailing

subfiles.about: Minister Wilson transmits ITU Bureau's explanation of frequency notifications under Washington and Madrid regulations.
subfiles.from: Hugh R. Wilson, American Minister, Bern
subfiles.summary: Transmits ITU Vice-Director Schwill's explanation that pre-Madrid notifications without station names retain original priority dates upon station allocation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4644 from Bern enclosing ITU Bureau letter on frequency registration

subfiles.about: Moore transmits the Bern Bureau report to FCC, questioning Japanese convention ratification dates.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Bern despatch and notes Japan had not ratified the 1927 Washington Convention when registering 8440 kc in 1928.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Anning S. Prall regarding convention applicability

subfiles.about: FCC acknowledges State Department letter regarding the mailing of the Bern report.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of letter advising that the Bern report was mailed on October 26.
subfiles.title: Letter from Anning S. Prall to Secretary of State acknowledging letter on Bern report

subfiles.about: FCC recommends withholding further representations on notification priorities until the Cairo Conference.
subfiles.summary: Advises against pressing international notification priority issues at Bern prior to the Cairo Conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Anning S. Prall to Secretary of State recommending postponement until Cairo Conference

subfiles.about: Press Wireless counsel requests State Department action on Japanese interference with three stations.
subfiles.summary: Details interference suffered by Press Wireless stations KHS, WRK, and KJY from Japanese stations JUD, JMO4, and JDK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Percy H. Russell, Jr. to Harvey B. Otterman requesting diplomatic representations
subfiles.to: Harvey B. Otterman, Treaty Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Moore informs Russell that instructions are being sent to Tokyo regarding Press Wireless interference.
subfiles.summary: States Embassy in Tokyo is instructed to seek elimination of interference affecting stations WRK, KJY, and KHS.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Percy H. Russell, Jr. outlining instructions to Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department requests status update from Tokyo on Press Wireless interference complaints.
subfiles.summary: Requests telegraphic report on status of interference, noting Press Wireless reports continued and expanding disruptions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 87 to American Embassy Tokyo requesting status report

subfiles.about: State Department instructs Tokyo Embassy to seek elimination of Japanese interference with Press Wireless.
subfiles.summary: Directs representations to Japanese authorities regarding interference caused by stations JMO4, JDK, and JUD.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 47 to American Embassy Tokyo instructing representations on Press Wireless interference

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo reports Japanese Foreign Office is investigating the Press Wireless interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports informal representations were made February 9 and the Foreign Office has referred the matter for technical investigation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 173 from Tokyo reporting Foreign Office investigation

subfiles.about: Moore informs Russell of Japanese Foreign Office investigation into radio interference.
subfiles.summary: Informs counsel that Japanese Foreign Office referred the interference complaint to appropriate authorities for investigation.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Percy H. Russell, Jr. reporting Japanese investigation

subfiles.about: Russell acknowledges report that Japanese authorities are investigating interference complaints.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges State Department letter and looks forward to receiving the results of the Japanese investigation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Percy H. Russell, Jr. to R. Walton Moore acknowledging status report
subfiles.to: R. Walton Moore, Department of State

subfiles.about: Navy Department requests diplomatic protest over Japanese station JXX interfering with naval frequencies.
subfiles.from: William D. Leahy, Acting Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.summary: Reports persistent interference to naval stations on 13,575 kc caused by Japanese station JXX; requests diplomatic representations.
subfiles.title: Letter from William D. Leahy to Secretary of State requesting action on Navy frequency interference

subfiles.about: State Department instructs Tokyo Embassy to protest excessive frequency deviation of station JXX.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Embassy to request correction of station JXX's frequency deviation violating Madrid Radio Regulations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 133 to American Embassy Tokyo regarding frequency deviation of station JXX

subfiles.about: Moore informs Secretary Swanson of diplomatic instructions regarding station JXX.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that Tokyo Embassy has been instructed by telegraph to request elimination of interference caused by station JXX.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Claude A. Swanson regarding action on Navy complaint
subfiles.to: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs Division recommends against pressing Tokyo unless Press Wireless reports ongoing interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Recommends taking no further action at Tokyo unless Press Wireless confirms that interference still persists.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Joseph W. Ballantine to Treaty Division regarding Press Wireless representations

subfiles.about: Otterman inquires whether Far Eastern Affairs recommends further telegrams to Tokyo regarding Press Wireless.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether FE considers it worthwhile to send another inquiry to Tokyo regarding Press Wireless interference.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Harvey B. Otterman to Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Tokyo representations

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports Japanese Communications Ministry is doing its utmost to eliminate radio interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese Communications Ministry is working to eliminate interference; Embassy will continue pressing for assurances.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 278 from Tokyo regarding Communications Ministry efforts

subfiles.about: Barnes recommends government cover telegraph costs for further representations on Press Wireless interference.
subfiles.summary: Notes Press Wireless reports continued interference but hesitates paying tolls; recommends charging telegram to Department.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles M. Barnes to Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding telegraph costs

subfiles.about: State Department instructs Tokyo Embassy that serious Press Wireless interference continues.
subfiles.summary: Advises Embassy of continuing serious interference and encourages continued efforts toward an early solution.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 163 to American Embassy Tokyo regarding continued interference

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits Japanese Ministry of Communications technical report and proposed remedial actions.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Japanese report addressing WRK/JMO frequency separation, suppressing JDK second harmonics affecting KJY, and curtailing JUD operations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 305 from Tokyo transmitting Communications Ministry technical report

subfiles.about: Moore instructs Ambassador Grew to thank Japanese authorities for investigating interference.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Ambassador to convey Department's appreciation to Japanese authorities for their efforts to eliminate radio interference.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1498 to Joseph C. Grew expressing appreciation
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Moore summarizes Japanese Ministry of Communications technical findings and remedies for Russell.
subfiles.summary: Details Japanese technical findings and measures regarding JMO frequency spacing, JDK second harmonic elimination, and curtailing JUD transmissions.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Percy H. Russell, Jr. summarizing Japanese findings

subfiles.about: FCC Acting Chairman Sykes requests State Department protest renewed interference from Dairen and Hsinking stations.
subfiles.from: Eugene O. Sykes, Acting Chairman, FCC
subfiles.summary: Requests diplomatic action to suppress station JDK's second harmonic at Dairen and keep station JMO-4 at Hsinking on carrier frequency.
subfiles.title: Letter from Eugene O. Sykes to Secretary of State requesting action on JDK and JMO-4

subfiles.about: State Department instructs Tokyo Embassy to demand elimination of JDK harmonics and JMO-4 frequency drift.
subfiles.summary: Directs Embassy to request elimination of JDK second harmonic and ensure JMO-4 maintains assigned carrier frequency.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 307 to American Embassy Tokyo regarding JDK and JMO-4 interference

subfiles.about: State Department informs FCC Chairman McNinch that instructions were cabled to Tokyo regarding KJY and WRK.
subfiles.summary: Confirms transmission of telegraphic instructions to Tokyo Embassy concerning interference suffered by stations KJY and WRK.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Frank R. McNinch regarding telegraphic instructions

subfiles.about: De Wolf explains omitting Manchukuo station locations in representations to avoid diplomatic awkwardness.
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Notes station locations in Manchukuo were omitted from complaints to avoid awkwardness, relying instead on ITU Japanese listings.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Francis Colt de Wolf regarding omission of Manchukuo station locations

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch acknowledges State Department's instructions to Tokyo Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges letter of September 7 regarding instructions sent to Tokyo concerning Press Wireless interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State acknowledging action on Press Wireless

subfiles.about: Siling transmits Press Wireless letter reporting persistent interference to station KJY.
subfiles.from: P. F. Siling, Assistant Chief, International Section, FCC
subfiles.summary: Transmits Press Wireless letter reporting continued severe interference to KJY caused by the second harmonic of JDK.
subfiles.title: Letter from P. F. Siling to Francis Colt de Wolf transmitting Press Wireless complaint
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf, Department of State

subfiles.about: Press Wireless reports persistent JDK harmonic interference and asks FCC for emergency tolerance relief.
subfiles.from: D. K. de Neuf, Superintendent of Operations, Press Wireless, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Reports severe interference from JDK harmonic forces off-frequency operation; asks FCC for temporary license tolerance expansion.
subfiles.title: Letter from D. K. de Neuf to Federal Communications Commission regarding KJY interference

subfiles.about: State Department directs Tokyo Embassy to renew urgent representations on station JDK harmonic interference.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Embassy to urge Japanese authorities to take immediate corrective action against the second harmonic of JDK.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 362 to American Embassy Tokyo renewing representations on station JDK

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports Japanese Foreign Office expects to advise definitely within a week on radio interference.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Foreign Office assurances that everything possible is being done and a definite reply is expected within a week.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 694 from Tokyo regarding Foreign Office assurances

subfiles.about: Moore informs FCC Chairman McNinch of Japanese Foreign Office assurances.
subfiles.summary: Relays Tokyo Embassy report stating Japanese Foreign Office expects to provide definite information within a week.
subfiles.title: Letter from R. Walton Moore to Frank R. McNinch reporting Japanese assurances

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch acknowledges report on Japanese assurances.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges State Department letter regarding Japanese efforts to eliminate interference to station KJY.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State acknowledging report on Japanese assurances

subfiles.about: Embassy Tokyo transmits Japanese findings asserting JDK harmonic is negligible and JMO-4 is on frequency.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Japanese report claiming JDK harmonic power is minus 37 decibels and attributing WRK interference to American frequency variations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 736 from Tokyo transmitting Japanese technical defense

subfiles.about: Sayre transmits Tokyo telegram containing Japanese technical findings to FCC.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copy of Tokyo telegram No. 736 containing the Japanese government's technical response for FCC comment.
subfiles.title: Letter from Francis B. Sayre to Frank R. McNinch transmitting Japanese report

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch states Japanese findings will be discussed with Press Wireless.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of Japanese technical report and states matter will be reviewed with Press Wireless.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State regarding consultations with Press Wireless

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch protests Japanese station JVP broadcasting on fixed service frequency 7510 kc.
subfiles.summary: Protests station JVP broadcasting on 7510 kc, causing severe interference to Press Wireless station WDD despite U.S. registration priority.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State regarding station JVP interference to WDD

subfiles.about: State Department instructs Tokyo Embassy to protest improper broadcasting by station JVP on 7510 kc.
subfiles.summary: Directs Embassy to demand cessation of JVP broadcasting on fixed frequency 7510 kc which interferes with station WDD.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 423 to American Embassy Tokyo protesting station JVP broadcasting

subfiles.about: Messersmith informs FCC Chairman McNinch that instructions were telegraphed to Tokyo regarding station JVP.
subfiles.summary: Confirms telegraphic instructions were sent to Tokyo Embassy regarding interference to station WDD by station JVP.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch regarding instructions on station JVP

subfiles.about: State Department asks Tokyo Embassy to expedite reply regarding station WDD interference.
subfiles.summary: Urges Embassy to expedite its report on representations concerning interference to station WDD.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 31 to American Embassy Tokyo requesting expedited reply on WDD

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits formal note and technical memorandum from Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits note from Seijiro Yoshizawa to E. H. Dooman enclosing technical report defending station JDK harmonic levels and JMO-4 frequency stability.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3469 from Tokyo enclosing Foreign Office note on radio interference

subfiles.about: Messersmith transmits copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 3469 to FCC Chairman McNinch.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copy of Despatch No. 3469 from Tokyo Embassy confirming previous telegraphic reports on Japanese radio interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch transmitting Despatch No. 3469

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch acknowledges receipt of Tokyo Despatch No. 3469.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges State Department letter transmitting copy of Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 3469.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State acknowledging Despatch No. 3469

subfiles.about: De Wolf requests previous despatches regarding Japanese telegraph discrimination be attached.
subfiles.summary: Requests Division of Communications and Records attach despatch of September 30, 1938 and other relevant previous documents.
subfiles.title: Routing slip from Francis Colt de Wolf requesting previous files

subfiles.about: Consul Gourley reports Japanese authorities urging American companies to use Japanese wireless over foreign cables.
subfiles.from: L. H. Gourley, American Consul, Kobe
subfiles.summary: Transmits Kobe Central Telegraph Office letter soliciting Dollar Steamship Lines to use government "Anten" wireless rather than submarine cables to preserve national exchange balances.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 64 from Kobe regarding Japanese pressure to route telegrams via wireless

subfiles.about: State Department transmits confidential copy of Kobe Despatch No. 64 to FCC.
subfiles.summary: Transmits confidential copy of Kobe Despatch No. 64 concerning Japanese requests that American companies use government wireless service.
subfiles.title: Cover letter transmitting Kobe Despatch No. 64 to Chairman, FCC

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports Japanese response on station JVP and requests details of U.S. interference observations.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese state JVP operates as secondary service and request specific observation dates and signal measurements in the United States.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 91 from Tokyo requesting detailed interference data on station JVP

subfiles.about: Messersmith transmits Japanese request for specific WDD interference data to FCC Chairman McNinch.
subfiles.summary: Relays Tokyo telegram requesting specific details regarding interference between stations WDD and JVP, including dates, areas, and intensity.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch requesting interference data

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch states the Japanese request for interference data was referred to Press Wireless.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges letter and advises that the Japanese request for detailed interference reports was referred to Press Wireless.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State regarding referral to Press Wireless

subfiles.about: FCC Chairman McNinch reports station JVP interference to station WDD has ceased.
subfiles.summary: Reports Press Wireless experienced no interference after February 7, indicating Japanese station JVP ceased or rescheduled conflicting broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank R. McNinch to Secretary of State reporting cessation of JVP interference

subfiles.about: Welles instructs Ambassador Grew to thank Japanese authorities for eliminating JVP interference.
subfiles.summary: Transmits FCC report of interference cessation and instructs Ambassador to express Department's appreciation to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1688 to Joseph C. Grew expressing appreciation for JVP interference cessation
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: FCC Acting Chairman Thompson reports daily recurring interference to station KJY from JDK harmonic.
subfiles.from: Frederick I. Thompson, Acting Chairman, FCC
subfiles.summary: Reports Press Wireless suffers daily traffic disruption from JDK harmonic; requests renewed diplomatic representations to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frederick I. Thompson to Secretary of State requesting action on renewed JDK interference

subfiles.about: State Department directs Tokyo Embassy to make renewed representations regarding JDK harmonic interference.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Embassy to inform Japanese authorities that JDK second harmonic continues disrupting station KJY and demand elimination.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 162 to American Embassy Tokyo demanding elimination of JDK harmonic

subfiles.about: Messersmith informs FCC that renewed representations have been telegraphed to Tokyo regarding station KJY.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that the American Embassy at Tokyo was instructed by telegraph to seek elimination of renewed JDK interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. Messersmith to Frank R. McNinch regarding renewed representations

subfiles.about: State Department urges Tokyo Embassy to expedite reply regarding renewed JDK interference.
subfiles.summary: Requests expedited telegraphic report on representations concerning JDK harmonic interference affecting Press Wireless station KJY.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Embassy Tokyo requesting expedited reply on station JDK
